speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Transport in light of the high prices of motorcycle COEs in recent biddings (a) whether the Ministry is concerned about the COE increase; (b) whether there is any market manipulation or any party who is keeping the COE prices up; (c) who bid for the nearly 400 bids that came in during the last moment before the tender closed at 4.00 pm on 8 August 2018; (d) whether this high COE price has adversely impacted those who rely on motorcycles as a mode of transport or for their job; and (e) whether the Ministry will consider increasing the bid deposit and shorten its validity period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We have seen this effect in Certificate of Entitlement (COE) bidding over the years and across all COE categories.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Member has suggested raising the COE bid deposit and shortening the validity period for motorcycle Temporary COEs (TCOEs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Both suggestions are not cost-free to the motorcycle buyers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: While raising the bid deposit may encourage dealers to be more prudent in submitting the bids, the higher bid deposit will raise costs for dealers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: If the Temporary COE (TCOE) validity period is shortened, dealers may need to maintain a larger inventory of motorcycles to meet demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: High business costs will mean higher prices for the buyers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Shorter TCOEs may also make it more difficult for buyers to obtain motorcycles immediately.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: In designing the COE system, we are mindful that motorcycle owners have different needs from owners of commercial and private cars.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Our COE system, therefore, sets aside a separate Category D for motorcycle buyers so that they need not compete with commercial and private car owners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The cessation of the contribution by Category D to the Open Category since May 2017 has helped to stabilise the supply of motorcycle COEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The majority of motorcycles also attract a much lower Additional Registration Fee (ARF) of 15% of the Open Market Value of motorcycles, compared to at least 100% for cars.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: COE prices fluctuate based on demand and supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We are mindful of the needs of motorcycle owners and businesses and are prepared to review the COE regulations if and when warranted.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: According to my resident, the COE bidding was $1 up to the last three minutes and then suddenly, 400 bids came in and pushed the COE to $5,514.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And a lot of my residents who depend on motorcycles for their transport as well as their job, like despatch rider, they are very concerned with this trend.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As I have mentioned in my reply, the last-minute bids that came in towards the end of the bidding cycle is a common practice, not just only in Category D COE but also in all classes of COEs, and this is not unusual.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In fact, COE prices, like I mentioned, fluctuate based on the supply and demand.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And like I have mentioned in my reply, the COE prices have come down from $8,000 to about $4,300 in the most recent September bidding cycle.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With the tiered Additional Registration Fee, we have a very progressive ownership tax structure that favours buyers of motorcycles with a low Open Market Value.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And I have also mentioned that we have already stopped the contribution of COEs from Category D to the Open Category.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This also increases the supply of motorcycle COEs in the market.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And, more importantly, besides our concern about the occasional increase in COE prices, the Government will also continue to enhance our public transport network and promote active mobility to create more commuting options for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I just want to know from the Senior Minister of State whether there are any other cases of such similar situation that happened, in terms of last-minute bids in the recent years.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Like I have mentioned, it is not an uncommon practice for bidders to come in at the last minute to bid for additional COEs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I think at this point in time, we do not have an intention to prevent that.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But, of course, the Ministry will continue to monitor the bidding patterns and, if necessary, we may make changes in the future.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: If not, can the Ministry study, just pay for what they bid for?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: That would prevent the last-minute bids coming in at high price.
